behavioral_concerns: follow up: Governed input fingerprint symlink check misses top-level symlink to directory and may allow path escape

evidence.summary: fingerprintOperationInputs final-component-only symlink check vs correct component-wise check; governed inputs share common top-level prefix enabling escape

governed inputs include file paths under projects/ and studies/ without separate validation of top-level directory prefixes; docs directory handling shows intended directory hash but inherits same missed intermediate check

theories.claim: fingerprintOperationInputs in internal/app/operations.go validates only the final joined governed input path for symlink, not every path prefix, so a top-level directory component such as `projects` or `projects/<project>` being a symlink to an external directory is followed and WalkDir hashes files outside the workspace (path escape)
theories.basis: Read-only inspection: fingerprintOperationInputs (operations.go:699-744) does `info, err := os.Lstat(path)` where `path=filepath.Join(root, rel)` and checks `info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink`, then for dirs runs `filepath.WalkDir(path, ... entry.Type()&ModeSymlink)`. This checks only the leaf and descendants. `os.Lstat` on a path with a symlinked intermediate directory follows the intermediate (POSIX Lstat follows intermediates, only leaf is not followed), so `Lstat(join(root,"projects/alpha/docs"))` where `projects` is a symlink returns the external target's directory info without error. Contrasted with the correct pattern in internal/app/usecases.go:199-212 rejectPreviewSymlink which iterates `for _, part := range split(rel) { path=join(path,part); Lstat(path); check ModeSymlink }`.
theories.verification_surface: read-only static code comparison of internal/app/operations.go:699-742 (fingerprintOperationInputs + hashOperationFile) vs internal/app/usecases.go:199-212 (rejectPreviewSymlink) and internal/app/web_usecases.go fingerprint basis; no execution, no file creation
theories.confirmation_condition: code shows Lstat applied only to final `filepath.Join(root,rel)` without per-component iteration, and WalkDir is called on the already-resolved external target, allowing intermediate directory symlink to escape workspace and be hashed via hashOperationFile (which uses os.ReadFile that follows symlinks)
theories.refutation_condition: code shows a loop that Lstats every prefix `root/part1`, `root/part1/part2`, ... for each governed rel before hashing and rejects any ModeSymlink, matching rejectPreviewSymlink
theories.inconclusive_condition: uncertainty about filepath.WalkDir handling of symlink root without runtime evaluation of Go stdlib behavior
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: compare source of fingerprintOperationInputs final-component Lstat and child-entry symlink check against rejectPreviewSymlink component-wise Lstat; inspect governedOperationInputs (operations.go:663-697) to confirm `projects/<project>/docs` and other file inputs share common `projects` prefix that is not itself a governed input

theories.outcome_reason: Static evidence confirms single-path Lstat at operations.go:703-712 and child-only WalkDir check at 720-721 versus component-wise loop at usecases.go:200-209. Governed inputs (operations.go:663-697) include deep file paths under `projects`/`studies` but not the top-level `projects` directory itself, so a symlink at `projects` (top-level directory) resolves via intermediate path resolution and is not detected, WalkDir then walks external directory and hashOperationFile reads outside files as governed inputs.
